metadata.title: Dresden Day Trip from Prague — Private Car & Chauffeur
metadata.description: A private day trip from Prague to Dresden in a Mercedes with your own chauffeur: the Frauenkirche, the Zwinger and the Old Masters, with the driver waiting and the drive back the same day.
metadata.ogTitle: Private Day Trip from Prague to Dresden

hero.label: Private Day Trip · Dresden
hero.intro: A private day trip from Prague to Dresden: a Mercedes and a chauffeur collect you at your hotel, drive you north across the German border, wait while you see the old town and bring you back the same day. From €{dayDresdenE} for the whole car, there and back.
hero.imageAlt: Mercedes V-Class on a day trip from Prague to Dresden

items.label: Price
items.value: From €{dayDresdenE} per car, there and back — not per person

items.label: Time there
items.value: Four to five hours for the old town and one museum

items.label: Included
items.value: Hotel pickup, chauffeur waiting on site, fuel and motorway tolls

paragraphs: Dresden, the capital of Saxony, was rebuilt stone by stone after 1945. The Frauenkirche was reconsecrated in 2005, the Zwinger palace and the Semper Opera stand again on the Elbe, and the Old Masters Picture Gallery holds Raphael’s Sistine Madonna.
The city is about two hours north of Prague by motorway. Most of the sights stand within a ten-minute walk of each other in the old town, so a day is enough to see them without rushing.
By private car you cross the border without changing trains and return when you choose, including after the last convenient train has gone.

items.title: The old town on foot
items.body: The Frauenkirche, the Procession of Princes, the Royal Palace, the Zwinger and the Semper Opera are close together. Your chauffeur drops you at the edge of the old town and waits nearby.

items.title: One museum, chosen in advance
items.body: The Old Masters Picture Gallery and the Green Vault are the two most visited. The Historic Green Vault admits visitors by timed ticket, so book it before you travel.

items.title: The Christmas market
items.body: From late November until Christmas Eve Dresden holds the Striezelmarkt, one of the oldest Christmas markets in Germany. It is a popular reason to make the trip in December.

items.title: A border without formalities
items.body: The Czech Republic and Germany are both in the Schengen area, so there is normally no border control. Carry your passport or national ID all the same.

items.title: One price for the car
items.body: €{dayDresdenE} in an E-Class (up to 3 passengers), €{dayDresdenV} in a V-Class (up to 6) and €{dayDresdenS} in an S-Class. The price is for the car, not per person, and covers the drive there, the wait and the drive back.

items.title: Child seats at no charge
items.body: Infant, toddler and booster seats are free. Tell us the children’s ages when you book and the right seats are fitted before pickup.

steps.label: How it works
steps.heading: Booking a day trip in four steps.

items.title: Book a return trip
items.body: In the booking form enter your Prague address and the destination, choose a return trip and set the return for the same day. A rough return time is enough — it can move on the day.

items.title: Choose the car
items.body: E-Class for up to three, V-Class for up to six with room to spare, S-Class for an executive day. You see the price for the whole car before you pay.

items.title: Meet your chauffeur
items.body: You receive the chauffeur’s name and phone number in advance. They collect you at your hotel or apartment door at the agreed time.

items.title: Take your time
items.body: The chauffeur waits near the centre while you visit. Call or message when you are ready and the car comes back for you.

editorial.label: Good to know
paragraphs: Many Dresden museums are closed on Mondays, and the Old Masters Picture Gallery is among them. Check the day before you fix the date.
Germany uses the euro, while the Czech Republic uses the koruna. Cards are accepted in most places in Dresden, but smaller cafés and market stalls often prefer cash.

Your chauffeur is a professional driver, not a tour guide: they know the road, where to drop you and where to wait, but they do not lead tours. Entrance tickets, meals and guided tours are not part of the price. If you would like a licensed local guide, book one for the hours you plan to be there and we time the drive around it.

faqs.q: How much is a private day trip from Prague to Dresden?
faqs.a: €{dayDresdenE} in an E-Class (up to 3 passengers), €{dayDresdenV} in a V-Class (up to 6) and €{dayDresdenS} in an S-Class. That is the price for the whole car for a daytime trip, there and back, with the chauffeur waiting while you visit. Fuel and motorway tolls are included. The exact fare for your date is shown in the booking form before you pay.

faqs.q: How long does the day trip take?
faqs.a: Plan about nine hours in total: roughly two hours each way and four to five hours in Dresden. Leaving Prague at 9:00, you are back around 18:00.

faqs.q: Does the chauffeur wait and drive us back the same day?
faqs.a: Yes. That is what a day trip is: the same car and chauffeur take you there, wait near the centre and drive you back to your Prague address. You do not look for a taxi or a train for the return.

faqs.q: Is a guide or entrance ticket included?
faqs.a: No. The price covers the car and the chauffeur. Tickets and guided tours are booked separately, and the chauffeur does not act as a guide. We are glad to time the day around a guide or a ticket slot you have booked.

faqs.q: Do we need passports for a day trip to Dresden?
faqs.a: Yes, carry a passport or national ID. Both countries are in the Schengen area and there is normally no check at the border, but police may ask for documents, and visitors from outside the EU need a valid passport and, where required, a Schengen visa.

faqs.q: How many people fit in one car?
faqs.a: Up to three passengers in an E-Class or S-Class and up to six in a V-Class. Larger groups travel in two or more cars. Child seats are free in every class.
